items.title: Nothing personal between me and Trump, Zelensky tells CNN
items.brief: After a bitter rift with Donald Trump left many in Ukraine fearing that the US president had swung behind Russia again, President Volodymyr Zelensky addressed the dispute head on: there’s nothing personal between me…

items.title: Taking back the algorithm: Social media platforms are restoring users’ control of their feeds
items.brief: As a new mom-to-be, my social media feeds have clocked me — funneling endless videos my way about pregnancy, nursery prep and birth stories, to the point of baby information overload.

items.title: KFC switches to Coke. But Pepsi’s still king at Taco Bell
items.brief: KFC dumped PepsiCo last week, but its sister chain Taco Bell announced Thursday it’s keeping the Mountain Dew Baja Blast maker on for another decade.

items.title: ‘Looksmaxxing’ streamer known as Clavicular pleads not guilty to rape charge
items.brief: The “looksmaxxing” livestreamer Braden Peters, better known by his stage name Clavicular , pleaded not guilty Thursday to charges that he raped a 17-year-old girl at his family’s Massachusetts home.

items.title: France reports first human case of livestock virus Shamonda after patient dies
items.brief: France on Thursday reported the first human case of the Shamonda virus usually found in livestock in a patient who later died, with authorities adding there was no risk to the general population at this stage.

items.title: She survived a school shooting. Now her children have, too
items.brief: “Mom, there’s a shooter,” Michelle’s fifth grader said through the phone.

items.title: Websites shut down globally after AI finds cybersecurity flaw affecting 70% of the internet
items.brief: Governments and companies around the world are racing to fix vulnerabilities revealed by artificial intelligence that could affect 70% of the world’s websites.

items.title: Construction on Trump’s 250-foot triumphal arch in DC could begin in just two weeks
items.brief: The Trump administration told a judge Wednesday evening that construction on the president’s controversial 250-foot triumphal arch could begin in just two weeks, days after the midterm elections.
